summary: Plan, monitor, and report youth and community projects with practical tools. Explore the five-day course outline and learning outcomes.
lede: Youth project management training covers turning community priorities into scoped initiatives, delivery plans, and outcome reports. Designed for youth project officers, community development workers, and programme coordinators, it provides practical methods for assessing needs, engaging young people, planning work and resources, monitoring results, and reporting outcomes. Participants practise Theory of Change, logical framework and workplan design, indicator tracking, safeguarding risk identification, and outcome reporting, with digital dashboards and evaluation methods also covered.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who coordinate youth programmes or community initiatives and need practical methods for planning, safeguarding, monitoring, and reporting project work.
modules: Theory of Change for Youth Projects
Participatory Rural Appraisal for Youth Needs
prerequisites: Prior experience supporting or coordinating a youth or community programme is useful. You should be able to work with basic project information such as activities, timelines, and budgets. No coding is required. Optional spreadsheet or dashboard exercises may use Microsoft Excel or Power BI; access to these commercial products may require an existing licence.
